answers.answer: SCOPe 2.08 (current release per /api/v1/) places all three in the CheY-like superfamily c.23.1, within the flavodoxin-like fold c.23 (class c). The supported relationship is a shared superfamily-level lineage: CheY-related response regulators are family c.23.1.1 (sunid 52173), the ornithine decarboxylase N-terminal 'wing' domain is family c.23.1.4 (sunid 52252), and the N-terminal domain of KaiA is family c.23.1.5 (sunid 82345; 1r8j chain A residues 2-135 = d1r8ja2). Superfamily membership supports a common evolutionary origin of the CheY-like core; fold membership alone (c.23) would not. The three are distinct families, so family-level homology, sequence identity, and function transfer are not supported. Only the KaiA N-terminal domain is in this lineage: the C-terminal region of the same chain (d1r8ja1, residues 177-282) is class a.186.1.1, a different all-alpha fold. Not supported by the classification: (1) phosphorylation-dependent signaling or phosphorelay for the KaiA N-terminal domain or the ODC wing, which needs experimental phosphorylation data and sequence analysis of the phospho-acceptor residue; (2) any catalytic role for the ODC N-terminal wing, since SCOPe assigns the PLP-dependent decarboxylase chemistry to the separate ODC major domain c.67.1.5 (sunid 53445); (3) any KaiA clock-regulation or KaiC-binding function, which requires functional and binding assays. Required external evidence for these claims: sequence alignment and conserved-residue analysis, mutagenesis, binding or phosphorylation assays, and enzyme kinetics. Limits: SCOPe domain assignments are representative (one chain, 1r8j, was used for KaiA), so other KaiA structures or domain boundaries could differ.
